delta: # Story 60 — Stale-write ref

usal speaks with one voice on the queue row (Story: CRM-95)

## Prerequisites

- **TIC
KETS-13-API (CRM-94)** must ship first. That story owns the 409 refusal (`RE
VISION_MISMATCH`) and the returning of the fresh revision on a successful write. This WEB story only unifies the on-screen behaviour of

the three queue-row controls that already handle the refusal.
- Familiarity with the existing per-control 409 branches on

the queue row (already shipped alongside `ticketAssign`, `ticketStatus`, `ticketCategory`).

---

## Story Goal

The three queue-row controls that
write (`ticketAssign`, `ticketStatus`, `ticketCategory`) already detect a 409 `REVISION_MISMATCH` and show their own `staleTitle`. Today each control
uses a slightly different sentence — two say “This ticket changed while you were looking at it”, one says “…while you were reading it”, and Arabic has a mat
ching split. Three sentences for one cause teach a user that there are three causes. The story is to reduce these three strings to **one shared string per
language**, keep the same recovery action across all three controls, and make sure the row picks up the fresh revision from a successful write so an agent’s second edit on the same row is not ref

used by their own first.

**Out of scope**

- Any `api/` change — CRM-94 owns the rule and the refusal.
- A fourth control. The queue row ke

eps the three controls it has.
- Any change to controls **off** the queue row (thread reply, ticket detail page). This story is scoped to `

TicketQueuePage.tsx`.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` — the three write controls live

here. Read the region around **lines 100–320**; the stale branches are at:
   - `stale` computed at **line 109** from `ass

ign.error?.code === 'REVISION_MISMATCH'`.
   - Assign stale block starting **line 186**, titled `t.ticketAssign.staleTitle` (**

line 190**).
   - Category stale title `t.ticketCategory.staleTitle` (**line 236**).
   - Status stale title `t.ticketStatus.staleTitle` (**line 305**).
   - Comment near **

line 343** about the row holding stale references after a write.
2. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` — the three current strings:
   - **line 276** `staleTitle: 'This

ticket changed while you were looking at it'` (under `ticketAssign`).
   - **line 342** `staleTitle: 'This ticket changed while you were reading it'` (under `ticketStatus`).
   - **line 356** `staleTitle: 'This ticket changed while you were loo

king at it'` (under `ticketCategory`).
   - Look at neighbouring keys (`staleAction`, `staleBody` if any) in the same three

sections — collapse all stale-related strings the same way.
3. `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — the mirrored strings at **

lines 230, 292, 306**. Same collapse in Arabic.
4. `web/src/pages/tickets/AssignTicket.test.tsx` — asserts `en.ticketAssign.staleTitle` at **lines 162 and 180

**. Update to the new shared key.
5. `web/src/pages/tickets/ChangeCategory.test.tsx` — asserts `en.ticketCategory.staleTitle` at **lines 173 and 190**.
6. `web/src/

pages/tickets/ResolveTicket.test.tsx` — asserts `en.ticketStatus.staleTitle` at **line 169**.
7. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` — the EN/AR parity check.

New shared keys must exist in both files with the same shape.
8. `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — every user-vis

ible string must come from a resource file (BR-6).
9. `scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` — script that verifies EN/AR parity; the shared key must satisfy it.
10. `web
/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts` — how row state is stored and mutated. Read all ~4 KB. Confirm how a successful write fl

ows the returned ticket (with its new `revision`) back into the row so a follow-up write on the same row is not refused as stale.
11. `web/src/pages/tickets/useAssignTicket
.ts`, `useChangeCategory.ts`, `useChangeStatus.ts` — read each (each ~1 KB). Confirm that the response body from the API returns the fresh `revision` and

that the caller (or `useTicketQueue.ts`) updates the row with it.
12. `scripts/criteria/tickets.md` — acceptance criteria under **TICKETS-13-WEB** (~line 397).

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **BR-5** (owned upstream by CRM-94): a write carries the revision it read; the

API returns 409 on mismatch.
- **BR-6**: every user-visible string comes from a resource file, in both languages.

**Current behaviour**

- Each of the three controls has its own `staleTitle` (and companion strings). Two English sentences vs

one; two Arabic sentences vs one. The recovery affordance offered is `window.location.reload()`.

**New behaviour**

- One

shared stale-refusal string per language, used by all three controls.
- One shared recovery affordance across all three controls (keep `window.location.reload()` —

see task 3 below).
- After a successful write, the row carries the new revision returned by the API so a second write on the same row is not refused by the first.
- The 409 refusal is presented as an **informational** state (“somebody else got there first, take

another look”), **not** an error. It must not be routed through the generic error banner.

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Introduce one

shared stale-refusal string set

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`

- Add a new namespace, e.g. `ticketStaleWrite`, next to the existing

ticket-write namespaces:
  ```ts
  ticketStaleWrite: {
    title: 'This ticket changed while you were looking at it',
    body:  'Nothing went wrong — som

ebody else got there first. Take another look.',
    action:'Look again',
  },
  ```
  Exact wording is the planner’s suggestion; match the tone of the existing `
ticketAssign.staleTitle` (line 276) and align with the acceptance-criterion phrasing “the ticket changed while it was being read and off

ers to look again”.
- Remove `staleTitle` (and any sibling `staleBody` / `staleAction`) from `ticketAssign` (line 276 region), `ticketSt

atus` (line 342 region), `ticketCategory` (line 356 region).

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

- Add the mirrored `ticketStaleWrite` block. Use one

Arabic sentence — collapse the two current variants at **lines 230, 292, 306**. Suggested:
  ```ts
  ticketStaleWrite: {
    title: 'تغيّ

رت هذه التذكرة أثناء نظرك إليها',
    body:  'لم يح
دث خطأ — سبقك شخصٌ آخر. انظر م

رة أخرى.',
    action:'انظر مرة أخرى',
  },
  ```
- Delete the three per-control stale strings at lines 230, 292, 306.

Both files must remain in lock

step so `parity.test.ts` and `scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` pass.

### 2 — Point all three queue-row controls at the sh

ared string

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

- Extract the per-control stale JSX into a single small internal component or helper (e.g. `ren
derStaleRefusal(t)` or `<StaleRefusal />`) so the three branches at **lines 186–195**, **236–…

` at **line 190**
  - `title={t.ticketCategory.staleTitle}` at **line 236**
  - `title={t.ticketStatus.staleTitle}` at **line 305**
  with the shared component

/ shared key `t.ticketStaleWrite.title`.
- The action button (currently `window.location.reload()`) is kept and centralised. See task 3.
- Do **not** change the
`stale` predicate at **line 109** — it stays a check on `assign.error?.code === 'REVISION_MISMATCH'`, and the equivalent for the
other two mutations. Preserve the guard at **line 197** (`assign.status === 'error' && !stale && assign.error`) so the generic error banner still h

ides when the refusal is a 409.

### 3 — Keep one recovery action across all three controls

The story is explicit: “if `window.location.reload()` is kept, ke

ep it everywhere; if it is replaced, replace it everywhere.”

- Keep `window.location.reload()` for this story — replacing it is a lar
ger UX change outside the point count. Route all three controls’ action button through the same handler in the shared component from task

2.
- Do **not** silently swap in a targeted refetch here; if the team later ch

ooses a softer refresh, that is a separate story so all three controls move together.

### 4 — Preserve fresh-revision propagation on

success

**Files:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts`, `useAssignTicket.ts`, `useChangeCategory.ts`, `useChangeStatus.ts`.

- Read each hook and
confirm the success handler writes the API response (including `revision`) back onto the queue row it mutated. If any of the three drops the revision on the
floor (returns before merging, or merges only some fields), fix it so all three merge the
returned row — key at minimum `id`, `revision`, `status`, `assigneeId`, `categoryId`, `updatedAt`. The
comment at **TicketQueuePage.tsx line 343** already flags that a row can go stale relative to itself; make sure the three success paths obey the same mer

ge shape.
- No new state shape. This is a consistency task: three success paths, one merge.

### 5 — Do not treat a 409 as a

failure surface

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

- Confirm each of the three controls filters the 409 out

of the generic error banner (assign already does at **line 197**). Apply the same `!stale` guard to the category and status branches if they lack it.
- The shared `
<StaleRefusal />` renders inside the row (as today), not as a toast or a red banner. Visually ne

utral, not red — reuse the same styling `ticketAssign` uses today.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Two controls on the same row race.
** Agent hits Assign, it succeeds and updates the row’s revision (task 4). They then hit Change
Status. Expected: the second write carries the fresh revision and is **not** refused. Enforced by task 4 mer

ges in the three hooks.
- **409 raced with a plain 500.** Only `REVISION_MISMATCH` shows the stale refusal;
any other error still uses the generic error branch — the `!stale` guard at **TicketQueuePage.tsx line 197** must apply to all

three controls.
- **User in Arabic locale.** The Arabic `ticketStaleWrite` must be the exact wording used everywhere. `parity.test.ts` catches a

missing key; `no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` catches accidental LTR wrapping.
- **Hardcoded f
allback string.** If any refactor introduces a bare English string (`'Refused: stale'` or similar), `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` will fail. Route

every user-visible word through `t.ticketStaleWrite.*`.
- **Third party mutates row while the reload button is being clicked.** Re

load always re-reads the queue; second stale is fine and shows the same string.
- **Old i18n keys still referenced somewhere.** After
removing `ticketAssign.staleTitle`, `ticketStatus.staleTitle`, `ticketCategory.staleTitle`, grep the whole `web/` tree for each removed key — every
hit must be updated or removed. Leaving one stale reference will break TypeScript typing on the `t` namespace when it is typed, or f

ail a test at runtime.
- **New control added later.** The shared `<StaleRefusal />` keeps the promise: ad

ding a fourth control means importing the same component and the same handler.

---

## Test Plan

1. **`web/src/pages/tickets/AssignTic
ket.test.tsx`** — replace both `en.ticketAssign.staleTitle` assertions (**lines 162, 180**) with `en.ticketStaleWrite.title`. Add an assertion that the “look

again” action is present using `en.ticketStaleWrite.action`.
2. **`web/src/pages/tickets/ChangeCategory.test.tsx`** — replace `en.ticketCategory.staleTitle` (**lines 173, 190**) with `en.

ticketStaleWrite.title`. Same action-button assertion.
3. **`web/src/pages/tickets/ResolveTicket.test.tsx`** — replace `en.ticketStatus.staleTit

le` (**line 169**) with `en.ticketStaleWrite.title`. Same action-button assertion.
4. **New test** in `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.test.tsx` (or a new file `StaleW
rite.test.tsx` next to the queue page) — mount the queue, force each of the three mutations to fail with a stub
bed `REVISION_MISMATCH`, and assert **the exact same title and body render** for all three. This is the guard against the string

diverging again.
5. **New test** in the same file — successful assign returns a ticket with `revision + 1`; a follow-up change-status on the same row does

**not** trigger the stale branch. This proves task 4.
6. **New test** — a non-409 error from any of the three controls still rout
es to the generic error branch (i.e. the stale block is not rendered when `code !== 'REVISION_MISMATCH'`). Guards

the `!stale` filter for all three controls.
7. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — should pass automatically because both files add

/ remove the same keys. Re-run to confirm.
8. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — should pass; run to confirm no bare English

leaked in.

All web tests are vitest. Do **not** rely on typecheck alone (the web suite does not run `

tsc` as part of `npm test` — see standing hints).

---

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema change. No API change.
- Half-applied state (only some
controls switched to the shared key): parity test still passes, but tests 1–3 fail loudly. Rollback is a plain revert of the two

`i18n` files and `TicketQueuePage.tsx`.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend tests:** `cd web && npm test` — expect

the three updated control tests and the new shared-behaviour test to pass, plus `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.
2. **Frontend build:** `c

d web && npm run build` — runs `tsc -b && vite build`; catches any dangling reference to a removed i18n key.
3. **i18n parity script:** `node

scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` from repo root.
4. **Regression — API untouched:** `cd api && npm test` — no failures. Confirms this

WEB story did not drift into API code.
5. **Regression — no AI attribution:** from repo root, `grep -R
niE 'copilot|chatgpt|claude|assistant|ai[- ]generated|ai[- ]assist' web/src

` returns nothing new introduced by this change.
6. **Manual smoke (optional):** run
`cd web && npm run dev`, open two tabs on the queue as different agents, edit the same ticket from one, then hit Assign /

Change Status / Change Category from the other — each shows **the same title and body** and the same “look again” affordance.

---

## Done Criteria

- [ ] One shared `

ticketStaleWrite` namespace exists in both `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` with `title`, `body`, `action`.
- [ ] The three per-control stale ke

ys (`ticketAssign.staleTitle`, `ticketStatus.staleTitle`, `ticketCategory.staleTitle`, plus any sibling `staleBody`/`staleAction`) are removed from both language files.
- [ ] All three queue-row controls
in `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` render the stale refusal from the shared source (same title, same body, same action

button) via one shared component / helper.
- [ ] The stale refusal is not rendered as a generic error; the `!stale` guard is applied on all three controls (currently only on assign at **line 197

**).
- [ ] On a successful write, the row picks up the returned fresh revision so a follow-up write on the same row is not refused by the previous one — verified by test

5.
- [ ] `AssignTicket.test.tsx`, `ChangeCategory.test.tsx`, `ResolveTicket.test.tsx` are updated to reference the shared key.
- [ ] A

new shared-behaviour test asserts the three controls render identical strings on a `REVISION_MISMATCH`.
- [ ] `cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both green; `scripts/verify-

i18n-parity.mjs` green.
- [ ] No `api/` file is modified in the diff.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for conf
irmation before proceeding to the next story.**
